paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the last bar, the lighter bar is 46.73%, and the darker bar is 0.11%, which is negligible in the image). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning reduces biases to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across community and healthcare when tuned on education and workplace scenario prompts.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the percentage of prompts generating biased responses before and after instruction tuning, categorized by contact context. The horizontal axis displays three context categories: "Sports," "Community," and "Healthcare," arranged from left to right. The vertical axis represents percentage, ranging from 0 to 70, with tick labels at 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, and 70. Each context category contains two bars, a lighter shaded bar representing the percentage of biased responses before instruction tuning, and a darker shaded bar representing the percentage after instruction tuning. The lighter bars are positioned at the base of the chart, with the darker bars stacked on top. The lighter shaded bars display values ranging from 7.45% for "Sports - No Contact Before" to 46.73% for "Healthcare - Negative Contact Before." The darker shaded bars display values ranging from 0.00% for "Community - Positive Contact Before" to 8.31% for "Sports - Positive Contact Before." Bars are not sorted, and no individual bars are visually emphasized. A legend identifies the color coding, with light blue representing prompts with no contact before, light green representing prompts with positive contact before, dark blue representing prompts with negative contact before, and dark red representing prompts with positive contact after.
